yoktra
(‘that which binds,’ ‘a rope’)
------------------------------------------
As a technical term used in वेदिच् सच्रिड़िचेस्, it indicates a cord of muñja grass (Saccharum sara), having three strands. It is tied round the waist of the patnī or the wife of the yajamāna (sacrificer), either by the आग्नीध्र priest or by the अध्वर्यु priest or even by herself. This rite is called patnīsaṁhanana. This makes her ceremonially fit for the sacrifice. During this rite she has to recite a मन्त्र from the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa (

).
A similar rope, called yoktrapāśa, is tied round the neck of the bullock which draws the cart containing the सोम creepers.
